intro: The Irregulars keep the rooms above the shop the way the detective left them, though he has been gone for years now and the violin on the mantelpiece has gathered no dust at all. Its single retuned string hums at dusk, and the notes stacked beneath it are addressed, in his hand, to whoever is clever enough to read them. To the untrained eye they look like ordinary scraps — a train ticket, a torn map, a list of the night's lodgers — but the landlady says each one has something left over, something that was never meant to fit. She has taken to pinning them to the wall with the oddments she finds in her apron, one small thing from each, in case whoever comes looking needs a trail.
echo: Means and opportunity are easy. The hard part is why.
